references.text: In Matthew's account, Peter follows Jesus "at a distance" to the high priest's courtyard, where he sits among the guards to see how it turns out ([ref:Matt 26:58|Matthew 26:58]). This is the parallel passage describing the same situation where Peter finds himself in the high priest's courtyard.

Mark tells us that Peter followed Jesus all the way into the high priest's courtyard and sat down with the guards, warming himself by the fire ([ref:Mark 14:54|Mark 14:54]). This is Mark's parallel to the same scene in the courtyard.

John describes how the servants and guards had made a charcoal fire because it was cold, and Peter stood there with them, warming himself ([ref:Joh 18:18|John 18:18]). This is John's parallel account of Peter by the fire in the courtyard.

Also in [ref:Joh 18:25|John 18:25], Peter is standing by the fire when he is questioned about whether he is one of Jesus' disciples. This shows the same situation where Peter sits or stands among the people around the fire.

In [ref:Mark 14:66-67|Mark 14:66-67], it is described that Peter was down in the courtyard warming himself when one of the high priest's servant girls noticed him. The scene by the fire provides the context for Peter's denial that follows.

The preceding verse ([ref:Luk 22:54|Luke 22:54]) sets the scene by telling us that they led Jesus to the high priest's house, and that Peter followed at a distance – which explains how Peter came to be in the courtyard where the fire was lit.

The following verse ([ref:Luk 22:56-57|Luke 22:56-57]) describes what happens while Peter is sitting by the fire: a servant girl sees him in the light of the fire and recognizes him, and Peter denies Jesus for the first time. The fire in the courtyard is thus the setting for the denial.
